intro: Lesson 24: Waves, weathering, mass movement and coastal erosion (2.1a). Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: Exam practice (portal printable): (a) Describe the features of a destructive wave. (2) (b) Explain two processes of coastal erosion. (4) (c) Explain why mass movement is common on clay cliffs. (3)
questions.a: (a) tall, steep, frequent, strong backwash (b) e.g. hydraulic action: air compressed in cracks; abrasion: rocks thrown at cliff (c) saturation adds weight, lubricates, slumping
questions.model: Teacher answers (a) live with the mark points shown.

questions.q: Annotate a cliff photo with processes acting on it.
questions.a: Waves, erosion, weathering and mass movement labelled

questions.q: Explain how climate change may increase coastal erosion.
questions.a: Rising sea levels and stronger storms bring more wave energy to cliffs; wetter winters saturate clay

questions.q: Explain how freeze-thaw weathering breaks up cliffs.
questions.a: Water enters cracks (1); it freezes and expands by about 9% (1); repeated freezing and thawing widens cracks until rock breaks off (1)
questions.model: Step 1: water in a crack. Step 2: freezes, expands. Step 3: repeated, crack widens. Step 4: rock falls.
